title.narrative: Empowerment for Poor Women & Adolescent Girls

description.narrative:
The Justice Development and Peace Commission is a faith based organization an organ of the church established to promote the social teachings of the Catholic church , protection of Human Rights and promotion of justice and equality as catalyst for peace and integral human development. This organ has been working in various spheres of human & community development, protection of Human rights {vulnerable children}, Savings and Internal Lending Communities (SILC), PROMIC (Micro-credit) and Civic education, Advocacy and ligation, prison welfare and social development. Under social development the commission has over the years been working on the protection support and provision of Micro-credit services to care-givers, Poor active women, PLWHA and Child Headed Homes.
JDPC, Abuja introduced Micro-financing project as a core component of economic strengthening activity for the Human Development programme. The micro-credit is a holistic programming approach that provides a strategy to increase low household income by providing people, primarily women, with income generating opportunities through access to microcredit, self-managed savings-led financial services. It has an improving effect to reducing poverty of rural community dwellers which has been a multiplier effect resulting to HIV/AIDS.
Justification: T o improve the livelihood and economic security the vulnerable persons (OVC/Care-givers, PLHIV, Active poor women) in and around Abuja Archdiocese.
To increase the household security poor communities within the Archdiocese through the accumulation of assets as a result of enhanced access to micro-financial services, access to basic insurance services and self manage savings-led services.
Primarily the project is aimed at developing individuals, households, villages or towns through empowerment of hundreds of poor individuals with entrepreneurial skills and willingness to work hard, and thus to make an efficient contribution to poverty reduction in families, villages and towns.
